text:
**Short answer:** For most people, the **Baseus EnerFill FC41** (25,000 mAh, 91.25 Wh) is the best pick. It's under the 100 Wh limit and can charge both a laptop and a phone. If you only need to charge a phone, get something smaller.

## My picks

- **Laptop and phone: Baseus EnerFill FC41**, $79.99. It outputs 140 W from one USB-C port and has two built-in USB-C cables. Code FC41 takes $12 off, per the source. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-enerfill-fc41-25000mah-145w)
- **Slim laptop-capable option: Baseus Blade H1**, 20,000 mAh (about 74 Wh, 100 W), $89.99. It's flat at 18 mm. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)
- **Phone only, lightest: Baseus PicoGo AM52**, 10,000 mAh (about 37 Wh), a magnetic Qi2.2 bank for $59.99. Code AM52 saves $6. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w-45w)
- **Cheapest laptop-capable option:** the INIU Cougar 20,000 mAh (73 Wh, 65 W) is listed at $46.99. The Anker Prime 26K ($229.99) and the UGREEN Nexode 25,000 mAh ($129.99) are pricier alternatives. Details are on the [Dealectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying), but I haven't given buy links for these because the source doesn't provide any.

Two caveats on these picks. The Baseus links come from Dealectric, which says it is paid when you buy through them. Their price and code testing was done on Oct 24, so check the price at checkout. The source also doesn't publish the FC41's weight.

## Rules to know before you fly

- **Carry-on only.** The FAA says power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Under 100 Wh (about 27,000 mAh).** The FAA sets no quantity limit for personal use below this. 101–160 Wh needs airline approval, and anything over 160 Wh is forbidden ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Airlines can be stricter.** According to the Dealectric table:
  - Southwest allows one power bank per customer and none in the overhead bin. It must be visible while in use, and you can't charge it from seat power ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)).
  - Delta and American allow two per passenger and no recharging the bank from seat outlets.
  - Some international carriers ban using a power bank on board at all.
  
  Check your airline's page before you go.
- **Cover the terminals** on a loose bank or keep it in its original packaging ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).
- **Avoid recalled models.** Anker recalled several models in June 2025 (A1647, A1652, A1681, A1689, A1257 and the PowerCore 10000).

The watt-hour formula is mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000. Use it if a bank doesn't print its Wh rating.
